main_text.p: stitiæ omitterentur ab hominibus, si modo vellent. Deus ergo decrevit illam voluntatem omittendi, voluntate absoluta, aut respectiva; si absoluta, habetur institutum: si respectiva, nempe decrevit, ut creaturæ vellent omittere actus justitiæ, modo vellent. 2. An non Deus multos credentes operaturos, siquidem satis superesset, multos actus justitiæ ex hac vita in beatitudinem vindicat? & tum actus justitiæ impedit Deus. Resipuissent Tyrii, si Deus signa adhibuisset, audiissent exteræ gentes Ezechielem, siquidem Deus ipsum ad vaticinandum misisset. At noluit Tyriis signa, noluit na-tionibus prophetas indulgere: Item Esai.63.17. 1.Sam.2.2 5. 3. Impeditor proprie est justitiæ, qui creaturam propendentem in actus justitiæ violentia alio torquet & avocat: at vero qui libere actus justitiæ omittunt, August.de civit.Dei lib.5.c.3& eosdem actus qui ut omitterentur, absolute Deus decrevit, sese libere impediunt, quo minus juste operentur, ideoque libere actus omittunt, & etiam necessitate decreti divini.

28. Non genio meo admodum arridet coacervare testimonia humana, huic sæculo ostentationibus delectanti unice placet, quædam tamen addo. August. 1. Si propterea quisquam res humanas tato Dei [?] (ut causæ, vide textum patris) tribuit, quia ipsam Dei vo-luntatem fati nomine appellat, sententiam teneat, & linguam corrigat. Et Enchrid.Enchir. 103 Nullus fit salvus nisi ille velit, & ideo rogandus est, ut velit, quia si ille velit, necesse est fieri. Etlib. 1.

page.notes: The first word "stitiæ" is a fragment at the head of the page, the start of the previous line cut off; it is kept as a fragment. "Resipuissent" is read with some doubt from the scan. "tato" in "tato Dei" is uncertain and marked. The page number 165 is printed at the top right; the running head is taken from the printed header "ABSOLUTI CONSOCIATIO". The right-hand reference "lib. 1." on the foot line is treated as a marginal note at the end of the text. Marginal notes sit in the right margin and are placed beside their lines.
